title: Wire up deal scoring and sorting logic across CrossModelSearchPage and backend

requirements.text: In `backend/main.mo`, ensure the `getCrossModelSearch` function computes `dealScore` for each result using the same average-price logic as `getDealScores`: for each unique make/model pair in the filtered result set, compute the average price across all non-archived listings for that make/model, then label each listing 'Good Deal' if its price is more than 10% below the average, 'Overpriced' if more than 10% above, and 'Fair' otherwise. Sort results by deal score tier first ('Good Deal' before 'Fair' before 'Overpriced'), then by price ascending within each tier. Verify this logic is fully implemented and not returning a hardcoded or empty `dealScore` field.

quotes: Make sure the deal scoring and sorting logic is fully wired in.

acceptanceCriteria: Calling `getCrossModelSearch` with a valid maxPrice and maxMileage returns listings with a non-empty `dealScore` field set to 'Good Deal', 'Fair', or 'Overpriced' based on the listing's price relative to the average for its make/model.
Listings priced more than 10% below the make/model average receive dealScore = 'Good Deal'.
Listings priced more than 10% above the make/model average receive dealScore = 'Overpriced'.
Results are sorted: 'Good Deal' listings appear first, then 'Fair', then 'Overpriced'; within each tier, results are sorted by price ascending.

requirements.text: In `frontend/src/pages/CrossModelSearchPage.tsx`, ensure the deal score badge rendering and result grouping are fully wired to the `dealScore` field returned by `useCrossModelSearch`. The 'Good Deal' section must only render listings where `dealScore === 'Good Deal'`. The badge colors must be: green/emerald for 'Good Deal', amber/yellow for 'Fair', red for 'Overpriced'. If a listing's `dealScore` is missing or empty, treat it as 'Fair'. Verify the sorting and grouping logic in the component matches the server-side ordering — 'Good Deal' first, 'Fair' second, 'Overpriced' third.

quotes: Make sure the deal scoring and sorting logic is fully wired in.

acceptanceCriteria: The highlighted 'Good Deal' section only contains listings whose `dealScore` field equals 'Good Deal'.
Deal score badges display green/emerald for 'Good Deal', amber/yellow for 'Fair', and red for 'Overpriced'.
Listings with a missing or empty `dealScore` are treated as 'Fair' and display the amber/yellow badge.
The result list is visually grouped: 'Good Deal' listings in a highlighted section appear before 'Fair' and 'Overpriced' listings.
Within each tier, listings are ordered by price ascending.
The secondary make/model text filter correctly narrows results across all tiers without disrupting the tier grouping.

constraints: Do not change the existing `getDealScores` backend function signature or logic.
Deal score computation in `getCrossModelSearch` must use the same threshold logic (10% above/below average) as `getDealScores`.
Do not modify any files under `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`, or `frontend/src/components/ui`.
nonGoals: Adding new deal score tiers beyond 'Good Deal', 'Fair', and 'Overpriced'.
Changing how deal scores are computed in `getDealScores` or any other existing backend function.
Adding deal score logic to any page other than CrossModelSearchPage and the backend `getCrossModelSearch` function.
Persisting deal score results or caching them in the backend stable map.
